key_insight: Cross-lingual transfer from Arabic and Persian can substantially improve biomedical machine translation for very low-resource Arabic-script languages, especially when using LoRA-based pivot adapters and adapter merging.
clinical_relevance: This could help expand access to biomedical information in under-resourced languages, but the results are not yet reliable enough for high-stakes clinical use in more distant language pairs.
method: LoRA fine-tuning of small decoder-only LLMs
Train domain-specific pivot adapters on Arabic and Persian
Compare few-shot prompting, 500-sentence supervised adaptation, and zero-data adapter merging
evidence_signal: The abstract reports CHrF++ gains, including near-pivot performance for Dari with 500 sentences (41.01) and meaningful improvement for Urdu (28.88), with adapter merging landing within 3.5 CHrF++ of supervised adaptation for Dari.
watch_item: Pashto and Sorani Kurdish remained too weak for safe clinical deployment, showing that transfer performance drops sharply when the target language is structurally distant from the pivots.
paper_title: Biomedical Machine Translation for Low-Resource Arabic-Script Languages via Cross-Lingual Transfer and LoRA Adapter Merging
